title: The Grain Road
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 4, with the party riding southwest from the sick village toward the source.
openLocation: Lordaeron trade roads between village depots and the routes feeding into Andorhal.
immediateObjective: Work backward along the grain trail until they find the road that holds the whole plague network together.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Sylvanas only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, read or infer.

Elves cannot feel the contamination. Every reading of exposure arrives through Jaina (spell light, staff, her marks on the map). Sylvanas sees the result and the mage's face, never the sickness itself.
Narration: Sylvanas thinks 'the mage' until Beat 7, where she catches herself thinking 'Jaina' and lets it stand. Not before. Aloud it stays 'Mage' (or 'Proudmoore' in front of others) all chapter.
No warmth. Their trust is work-first. Respect is practical: she uses Jaina's read to choose the road.
Jaina's hands: left raw and wrapped, right dead since Ch2; hand-reading is banned. Readings go through spell light and the staff.
The overseer lies, is alive, and is gone when they return. Never bring him back after Beat 6.
The Barov name is proof of connection, not guilt. Sylvanas refuses to blur that line, and the narration must not blur it either.

The old carter is a nagging memory only. No proof, no pattern. Jaina does not pre-empt the snag; it is Sylvanas's alone. He must not be identified with or as the young grain-man with the cart. His one link to that man is that he asked after him, and that stays a question.
No Mal'Ganis naming. No Kel'Thuzad naming. No certainty about who designed the plague.
No counted time in dialogue ('two breaths'). Orders by event.
Grain-as-loud-carrier is established (Ch4). Do not re-prove it; the chapter is about scale and the road, not about the sickroom. Register is paper, records, road, not another sickroom.
Neral and the fourth ranger are gone; the two empty places in the line are a callback, not a new image.
Neral stays on the northbound warning line. Do not bring her back.
Cyndia must have a real function (counting, records, perimeter reads) before her Ch10 shift. She has been thin for two chapters.
Lyriel rides at Jaina's knee when the road allows and jokes where Cyndia won't. She calls Jaina 'Jaina' (Ch4 landed this).
Do not name the village from Ch4 unless the Ch4 final does. It is unnamed on the page; refer to it as the village / the one with the granary fire.

Timeline and the rut read: the last rain fell before dawn on the morning they left the village (Ch4). No new rain on the page until after B6, or the rut read breaks. The overseer's 'two days ago' must fall after that rain (see timeAnchor on B4-B6).

Jaina's marks: the right hand is dead and only two fingertips of the wrapped left hand work (Ch4). Her marks on the map go down clumsily with those two fingers, or another hand makes them at her word (Tobin's slate in Ch4 is the precedent). 'Ink-stained fingers' belong to clerks, Sylvanas or Cyndia, not to Jaina.

Arthas and Strahnbrad are new on the page. Sylvanas needs an on-page source for the army being at Strahnbrad before B9: road talk from the S1 innkeepers and merchants, or the B6 toll-keeper. The writer picks one.
Cyndia's turned head after the carter's wagon (Ch3) belongs to Ch9 and Ch15. Nobody raises it in Ch5, and Sylvanas does not ask Cyndia about the carter.

povKnowsAtOpen: Someone organized the wagons and is killing loose ends.
The trail points southwest toward Andorhal (ANDORHAL stencil on the sacking, folded in her coat; Brask: three days by cart down the grain road; everything in the south goes through it).
Most towns are only in the early stage of the sickness, but Millhaven was hit hard.
They stopped the grain in time at the sick village, and it lives.
Jaina can read contamination before other people know a place is sick.

The girl's 'newer grain seller' at Millhaven and the sick village's young man with the cart are, she and Jaina judged in Ch4, one man. The old carter on the Millhaven road asked after a young grain man too. That question is the carter's only thread to anything, and it proves nothing.
A watcher was placed in the granary, carried poison sewn into his collar and died rather than talk (Ch4): the network is organized and wastes its people.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Who is really running the trade route.
Whether the Barovs built the plague, helped cover it, or know nothing.
Whether the old carter matters or just looks suspicious in hindsight.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No certainty that the Barovs are guilty.
No sudden warmth between Sylvanas and Jaina.
No proof that the old carter is the creature behind the plague.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: A live regional network is moving grain and cleaning the road ahead of them; they arrive after each move.
Andorhal is the hub the routes pinch toward.
The Barov name is all over the grain paper: connection, not proven guilt.
The depot overseer lied; it cost them a day; he is alive and gone.
The southern supply road is the best approach and runs straight through Arthas's war near Strahnbrad.
Sylvanas carries the old carter forward as a nagging memory, unmatched to anything.
Arthas's army is at work near Strahnbrad against the orcs (from road talk or the toll-keeper); Sylvanas expects it to rank the grain below the orcs.

pov: She starts the ride treating this like road work: map the depots, read the wagons, find the break in the trail.
The records get too big and too strange for tracking alone, and she has to lean on Jaina's magic to keep the hunt moving.
The overseer's lie costs them a day. Sylvanas reads it from the road, a day late.
By the end, Sylvanas is no longer just tolerating Jaina's help. She is using Jaina's read to choose the road ahead.

beats: Sylvanas opens still half-expecting theory and softness from Jaina.
Jaina keeps matching the work: fast reads, quick corrections, no pride when the facts change.
Sylvanas's respect turns practical. She stops thinking the mage and starts thinking Jaina.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They start out doing the same job from different angles, still sharp with each other.
The miles force a clean split of labor: Jaina finds the invisible trail, Sylvanas follows the paper and the road.
By the end, they are still not gentle, but they are finally trusting the same hunt.

castAndHandoffRules.Lyriel: Still riding point and perimeter. When the road allows she rides at Jaina's knee, and she jokes where Cyndia won't.
castAndHandoffRules.Depot overseer: Alive. He lies to them and is gone when they come back. Do not bring him back.
castAndHandoffRules.Neral: Not with the party. She stays on the northbound warning line.
castAndHandoffRules.nextChapterStarts: Chapter 6 opens with the same four riders on the southern road, heading toward the military zone near Strahnbrad before Andorhal.

factsLocked: The party is on the southern road toward Andorhal.
Their chosen road runs through Arthas's military zone near Strahnbrad.
The Barov name keeps appearing in the grain records, but guilt is still unproven.
They lost a day to the overseer's lie.
The old carter is a nagging memory for Sylvanas, not yet a pattern.
factsNotEarned: Open emotional closeness between Sylvanas and Jaina.
Proof that the old carter is the same creature behind the plague.

scenes.title: The Paper Trail
scenes.sceneFunction: Sylvanas and Jaina turn scattered sickness into a road map and realize they are tracking a network, not one bad village.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: They know grain is the carrier and are riding southwest down the grain road from the village, the ANDORHAL square folded in Sylvanas's coat. It is the same day they left (Ch4 dawn, after the rain); Jaina has come off an all-night ward vigil and is spent. Two empty places at the back of the line. Jaina's hands are wrapped (left split and rebound, right dead). Sylvanas still calls her 'Mage' aloud and thinks 'the mage'.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas starts out treating the hunt as road work she can do alone with paper; the scale outruns her method and she has to put the mage's read on the table beside her ledgers.
scenes.enrichment: Thalassian horses stay calm near arcane hum and road rhythm (project notes), so they carry the party through depot yards and ward-lit stops without drama; hot breath, foam, snort after a hard push. Grain-trade texture (tally sticks, depot sack stencils, toll books, inn day-books) is period-generic medieval trade practice, written from general knowledge, no web search run. Canon geography note: Andorhal sits in the Western Plaguelands south of Tirisfal; Brill is in Tirisfal Glades; Strahnbrad is in the Hillsbrad foothills. The outline's compression of these into one road system is an authorial choice and is kept.

beats.goal: Stop treating the plague like a rumor and work it like freight: pull ledgers, manifests, inn books and clerks' tallies at each depot stop, and lay them beside Jaina's readings of which places are deep in exposure and which are only starting to turn.
beats.conflict: Paper and magic arrive as two competing guesses. Clerks hedge, books disagree on weights and dates, Jaina's marks do not sit on Sylvanas's route lines until they force the two to share one page.

outcome.summary: Millhaven's grain route matches dozens of other towns' routes, and the two methods finally build one map instead of two guesses. The hunt stops looking local.

beats.valueShift: two competing guesses -> one shared map
newOnPageInformation: Millhaven's grain route matches the routes of dozens of other towns
Jaina can sort towns into deep exposure versus just turning, and her sorting agrees with the paper
The problem is regional, not one village's line
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Where the center of it sits
sensoryAnchors: horses tethered outside hot little offices
beats.interiority: road work, and she can do road work; still half-waiting for the lecture, the theory, the softness; the mage's marks keep landing where the ledgers say, and she would like them not to; fine, one map
beats.castFunction: Cyndia counts: wagon tallies, depot names, town frequency, so she has work on the page. Lyriel keeps clerks talking.
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: one map shows the spread is wider than one village, so each new ledger raises the stakes.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 1, afternoon: the first depot office down the grain road, past the ford, hours after leaving the village.
beats.continuityNote: Opening beat. It must be a scene in one specific office over one specific ledger, with the two methods arguing, not a summary of 'they began working it like freight'. One depot's books list dozens of destinations, so 'dozens of towns' does not need dozens of stops. The ANDORHAL stencil and Brask's 'everything in the south goes through Andorhal' are known: callback anchors only, no re-explaining. Jaina is post-vigil; her reads are short and staff-only. Partnership bullet 1 needs one sharp exchange between them here. If the ford is passed, the carter does not surface there: B8 owns him.
beats.verifierModification: Added timeAnchor, tension and weight, continuity notes. Interiority extended so the Jaina arc's first bullet (half-expecting theory and softness) is planted here and paid in B7.

beats.goal: Narrow the map by working each new ledger until one regional depot stands out as the place the routes feed.
beats.conflict: Each ledger makes the picture worse. Repeated town names, layered notes, Jaina's marks over Sylvanas's route lines: one table becomes a mess, and the center stays buried under too many routes.

outcome.summary: They learn the poisoned grain is moving through a whole regional network, dozens of settlements, Lordaeron's trade roads used like a weapon. They cannot say which depot matters most, so they push for the regional depot that should finally narrow the map.

beats.valueShift: a bad village -> a weaponized road system
newOnPageInformation: Dozens of settlements are touched
Lordaeron's trade roads are the delivery system
A regional depot ahead should narrow the routes
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How far the spread already goes
sensoryAnchors: lamp or window light on paper
beats.interiority: records too big and too strange for tracking alone; her lines, the mage's marks, same table; leaning on magic she cannot check herself, and she lets it stand because the marks hold up
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: they ride for the regional depot that should narrow the map.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 2: several stops down the road and its side roads, one table at the end of it.
beats.castFunction: Arc requirement (Jaina bullet 2, Partnership bullet 2): the clean split of labour shows here. Jaina finds the invisible trail, Sylvanas follows the paper and the road. Somewhere in this beat Jaina revises one of her marks the moment the paper contradicts it, fast and without pride, and Sylvanas notes it. Cyndia keeps the count of town names.
beats.continuityNote: Millhaven as a late stage of a pattern along the grain road is settled (Ch4); this beat widens it, it does not re-prove it. Compress the miles. This beat must not replay B1's note (methods agree); its turn is scale, from a bad village to a weaponised road system. If the Strahnbrad source comes through road talk, this is its place.
beats.verifierModification: Added the arc requirement for Jaina's quick correction (outline Jaina bullet 2 had no beat delivering it), weight, time anchor and continuity.

beats.emotion: Cold recognition under the tiredness: this is not an old crime being studied.
beats.dilemma: Keep working each depot methodically, or treat the next stop as a race against people already moving grain and cleaning the road ahead of them.
beats.decision: She treats the next stop as a race. She pushes the pace and tells the line why, by event.
beats.valueShift: studying a crime -> chasing a live operation
newOnPageInformation: The network is active; they arrive after each move, never before it
Someone may already know they are coming
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the next depot will still have records when they reach it
sensoryAnchors: Lyriel at Jaina's knee laughing over a clerk's handwriting
beats.interiority: arrived after every move; the lag is a pattern; someone could be reading the road behind them; the trees on both sides are suddenly a worse position
beats.castFunction: Lyriel makes Jaina laugh about a clerk's handwriting while Cyndia keeps her eyes on the trees. Contrast of registers, no commentary on it.
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the race starts, and they ride through the dark for the regional depot.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 2, evening into dark: they ride on rather than stop.
beats.continuityNote: The organized network was proven by Tam in Ch4; what is new is that it is live and ahead of them. Evening damp, not rain (see constraints). Lyriel's clerk joke and Jaina's laugh: Lyriel says 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not laugh. Order of march: Sylvanas front, Cyndia left, Lyriel right (at Jaina's knee when the road allows), Jaina middle, two empty places behind: a callback, not a new image.
beats.verifierModification: Transition relabelled; time anchor, tension, weight and continuity added.

scenes.title: The Cleaned Depot
scenes.sceneFunction: The next depot has been wiped clean, and the man left in charge of it lies to them.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: They are chasing a live network, not just mapping old damage, and have ridden through the night to treat the next stop as a race. Nobody has warned them that evidence is being erased ahead of them.
scenes.arcPressure: The chapter's main stance test: Sylvanas takes an answer because the clock is running, an excuse she would flay a ranger for, and pays a day for it.
scenes.enrichment: Overseer tells (ink on cuffs, readiness of the answer, fresh ash in a stove on a warm day) are the plain-sight clues: write them without comment. Road reading by wheel ruts after rain is standard tracking practice for a Farstrider; laden wagons cut deeper and keep their edges until the next rain. Toll-keepers keep day-books, which is how the lie is checked. General knowledge, no search. Verifier: B6 split into B6 (the road and the empty house) and B6a (the ash pit), so the scene now runs goal, conflict, disaster, sequel.

beats.goal: Reach the regional depot in time to seize its books and grain before anyone moves them.
beats.conflict: They are already late. The books are gone, the grain is gone, and the warehouse is too clean to trust, swept like a place made quiet on purpose.

outcome.summary: Nothing to seize. Someone has erased the evidence ahead of them and understands exactly what matters in this building, which means the road is being watched. They stop looking for books and start looking for the keeper.

newOnPageInformation: Books and grain both removed; the building is deliberately clean
The enemy knows what matters in a depot and is erasing it ahead of them
Someone is left in charge
sensoryAnchors: warehouse quiet that feels made rather than natural
beats.interiority: swept; nobody sweeps a depot this clean in a hurry, someone swept it carefully; who told them to expect us; no, not yet, find the man who holds the key
beats.castFunction: Cyndia works the perimeter and reports what the yard says; Jaina checks for residue with the staff and finds the building thin, not dirty.
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: if the depot was cleaned, the keeper left behind knows who did it.
beats.continuityNote: Jaina reads by staff only. Elves cannot feel the contamination: 'thin, not dirty' arrives as Jaina's report, never as Sylvanas's sense.
beats.verifierModification: Transition relabelled; time anchor and continuity added.

beats.goal: Get a usable direction out of the one man left at the depot before the trail goes cold.
beats.conflict: The overseer is alive at his desk, pleasant and pale, with an answer that arrives too ready. Jaina reads no magic on him, only a frightened man. Sylvanas puts the fear down to the empty depot, and with the clock running she takes his word.

outcome.summary: He gives them a quick, plausible story: books to the regional office last week, last grain wagons north on the road toward Brill two days ago. They have a direction and ride north on his word. It is a lie, and the cost lands later.

beats.valueShift: no lead -> a lead she should not trust
newOnPageInformation: The overseer's claimed account: books went to the regional office last week
His claimed account: last grain wagons left on the north road toward Brill two days ago
Jaina finds no magic on him, only a frightened man
sensoryAnchors: an answer that comes too ready
fresh ash in a stove on a warm day
beats.interiority: the ash on a warm day, and she saw it; fear, but fear of what; the clock is running and she lets the explanation do the work of the question
beats.plannerWarning: The ash, the cuffs and the readiness are plain-sight clues. The writer must show them and never comment on them as clues; Sylvanas registers them and files them under the empty depot.
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: they ride north on his word.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 3, mid-morning. The overseer's 'two days ago' is day 1, after the pre-dawn rain, so wagons that really left would have cut fresh ruts.
beats.continuityNote: Fair play: the ash, the cuffs and the ready answer must be on the page in plain sight, and the next line should give the reader something more interesting to look at. Jaina reads magic, not fear: 'no magic on him' is her finding, and the fear is what Sylvanas sees. Sylvanas's decision to take his word is hers alone, a choice made under the clock, not a trick played on her.
beats.verifierModification: Time anchor fixes the rut logic: if 'two days ago' fell before the last rain, B6's rut read would prove nothing.

beats.goal: Reach the grain wagons on the north road toward Brill.
beats.conflict: The road itself tells Sylvanas he lied: no heavy wheel ruts newer than the last rain, and a toll-keeper who has seen no grain wagons in a month. They ride back hard and lose the day. The depot is locked, the overseer gone, alive, his house emptied in a hurry.

outcome.summary: No wagons, a day gone, and the one man who knew is gone too. All that is left is the stove and the ash pit, which she saw on a warm day and filed under the empty depot.

beats.valueShift: a lead -> a lost day and an empty chair
newOnPageInformation: No heavy wheel ruts newer than the last rain on the north road; the toll-keeper has seen no grain wagons in a month
The overseer is gone, alive; his house emptied in a hurry; the depot locked
sensoryAnchors: a hurried house: drawers out, a door left open
beats.interiority: no ruts; none; took his word because the clock was running, the excuse she would flay a ranger for; fresh ash on a warm day, and she saw it; ride
beats.castFunction: Cyndia confirms the road read; Lyriel takes the toll-keeper. Sylvanas owns the error flat, to herself, and moves.
beats.plannerWarning: Compress the north ride and the ride back to a few marks (ruts, toll-keeper, hard ride). The overseer does not appear again after this beat in any form.
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the stove and the ash pit are the only witnesses left, and she goes down on her knees to them.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 3 into day 4: north all day to the toll by evening, back hard through the night, the depot locked by first light on day 4.
beats.continuityNote: The rut read rests on the Ch4 rain before dawn on departure day; Sylvanas knows when it fell. If the toll-keeper is the Strahnbrad source, he tells her what traffic he has seen instead: soldiers, not grain.
beats.verifierModification: Split outline beat 6 into B6 (disaster: the road shows the lie, the day lost, the overseer gone) and B6a (sequel: the ash-pit search, the Barov name, connection not guilt). The original beat held two value shifts and five locations. The split gives the chapter's worst moment its own sequel. Inside lines divided: the self-indictment goes to B6, the Barov temptation to B6a.

beats.emotion: Cold, self-directed anger held down into work.
beats.dilemma: Let the name on the paper settle it (guilty is simpler, and it would point the road), or hold the line between connection and guilt and take only what the paper proves.
beats.decision: She holds the line. The paper proves connection and a hub; she takes the hub (Andorhal) as the destination and refuses to call the Barovs guilty, even inside her own head, where she has to keep saying it.
beats.valueShift: a lost day -> a destination and an ugly name
newOnPageInformation: Torn slips and broken seals recovered from the stove and the ash pit
The routes pinch toward Andorhal
The Barov name is on the paper again and again: proof of connection, not proof of guilt

sensoryAnchors: slips laid out in rows on the floorboards

beats.castFunction: Cyndia sorts and counts the scraps alongside her (records work before her Ch10 shift). Jaina reads the char for residue and does not gloat or console. If the Barov house needs placing as a Lordaeron noble name, Jaina may place it (a Proudmoore knows the houses), without arguing guilt.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 4, from first light: hours at the stove and the ash pit.
beats.continuityNote: Andorhal was named on the page in Ch4 (stencil, Brask) with Jaina's doubt ('or where he wanted us to think it came from'). The scraps turn that doubt into a hub the paper confirms; the stencil is a callback. The Barov name is new on the page. No Mal'Ganis, no Kel'Thuzad, no designer named.
beats.plannerWarning: Narration must not blur connection into guilt either. The name appears; the verdict does not.
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: they have a destination and a day less to reach it, and the final road in has to be chosen from all of it laid out at once.
beats.verifierModification: Added by the B6 split (see B6). The outline's beat 6 content and Inside line are preserved across the two beats.

scenes.title: The South Road
scenes.sceneFunction: They lock the route to Andorhal, Sylvanas fully accepts Jaina as a working partner, and the old carter clue comes back.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Day 4, night. They have the Barov name, Andorhal as the hub, and a road being cleaned ahead of them. A day is lost. Sylvanas has owned the overseer error to herself and refused to turn the name into a verdict.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas stops holding Jaina at arm's length inside her own head and uses Jaina's read to choose the road. Aloud still Mage.
scenes.enrichment: Strahnbrad is a Hillsbrad-foothills town and the staging ground for Arthas's campaign against the orcs (Warcraft III canon, from general knowledge, no search run). The outline places the army's road on the way to Andorhal; kept as authorial geography. Hold the army as distant dust and rumor in this chapter; the ride into the zone is Chapter 6.

beats.goal: At a midnight stop, fuse the paper trail with Jaina's magical map into one working picture of the network and its roads.
beats.conflict: Too much paper, a day lost, tired hands, and Sylvanas's own habit of waiting for the mage to need handling before she will rely on her.

outcome.summary: The road pattern snaps into place. Jaina gives hard, useful answers without needing to be handled. Sylvanas catches herself thinking 'Jaina' and lets it stand. The read she now trusts is the one B9 turns into a road.

beats.valueShift: holding her at arm's length -> using her read
newOnPageInformation: The paper trail and Jaina's magical map fit into one pattern of roads
Jaina's reads are hard and useful and need no handling
The routes converge on Andorhal as the hub
stillUnknownAfterBeat: What the Barov connection really means
sensoryAnchors: Cyndia and Lyriel outside the perimeter
quiet concentration instead of another argument
cold night air at the door
beats.interiority: no handling needed, which is rare in a human mage and rarer in a Kirin Tor one; catches herself thinking the name and lets it stand; work, and only work; still half-waiting for the softness, and annoyed it hasn't come
beats.plannerWarning: First on-page 'Jaina' in Sylvanas's head. Narration changes from 'the mage' to 'Jaina' here and stays changed afterward. Dialogue still 'Mage'. Do not announce the change; let it land in the narration and do not comment on it beyond the Inside line.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional carryover: the pattern now looks deliberate, and a deliberate pattern makes one odd old man on the Millhaven road sit wrong.
beats.timeAnchor: Night of day 4: the midnight stop, south of the depot.
beats.continuityNote: Ch4 left them a working pair with a shared win and no warmth; Jaina already thinks 'Sylvanas' (Sylvanas does not know). This beat is the matching hinge on Sylvanas's side, internal only. Aloud: 'Mage'. No thanks, no softening, no shared look given weight.
beats.verifierModification: Outcome reworded so the road choice itself lands in B9, where the outline places it, with B7 supplying the read. Transition relabelled from a sensory carry with no sensory object to the causal emotional carry.

beats.emotion: Irritation at a memory she cannot make into anything.
beats.dilemma: Treat the old carter as one odd man on a road, as she has told rangers a hundred times, or as the first piece of a pattern she cannot prove.
beats.decision: She files him as a memory, not a pattern, and carries him forward without pretending he is proof.
beats.valueShift: clean certainty about the network -> an unplaced snag
newOnPageInformation: The old carter from the Millhaven road comes back to her: his empty wagon, his question about the grain-man
The operation is too controlled for the encounter to sit easily

How the depot knew to expect them

the echo of a polite flat voice
the irritation of missing something important

beats.plannerWarning: The carter is observable-only. Do not have Sylvanas decide what he is, and do not have Jaina or Cyndia raise him. Correct handles from the Ch3 page: an empty wagon ('Empty going up, full coming down', her own thought then); 'Nothing for me here, then', after which he drove on north, up the empty street into the dead village rather than turning for home; his question after a young fellow with a grain cart, 'coming down from your way'; 'well enough on market day' against five days dead. Do not conflate him with the young man with the cart.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional carryover: the nagging memory rides with her into the choice of road.
beats.timeAnchor: Same night, after the map settles.
beats.continuityNote: Earlier plan text said the wagon was 'heading away from Millhaven'. On the page it drove north, deeper into the dead village. Use the page. Guard the Ch3 plant: Lyriel told the carter they would watch for the grain man going south. Sylvanas may set the carter beside the unanswered 'who told the depot' in the same quiet, but she must not draw the line from Lyriel's answer to the leak. That link is for a second reading, not for her. If the farewell words recur, they recur only in her own head; Cyndia's corroboration belongs to Ch9.
beats.verifierModification: plannerWarning corrected against the Ch3 prose (the wagon's direction); guard added for the Lyriel-answer plant; callback annotated.

beats.dilemma: The main highway is the open way and the one a watched road would predict; the southern supply road is the best path but runs straight through Arthas's war near Strahnbrad.
beats.decision: They choose the southern supply road into Andorhal, off the main highway. The choice rests on Jaina's read from B7: Sylvanas takes it without asking for proof, which is the arc landing. She warns Jaina what the army will do: pour its strength into the orcs it can already see and rank the poisoned grain below them.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch4 ends in Jaina's POV at the dawn after the rain: the village lives, Brask writes their names in his ledger, Sylvanas shows the ANDORHAL square cut from the loft sacks and folds it back into her coat ('Either way, it's the road he drove'), and the four ride down through the village in crest order with two empty places at the back. At the split past the brook the staff leans toward the ruts, and Sylvanas turns onto the grain road without a word.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same day, hours later, same four riders in the same order. Jaina is spent from the all-night ward vigil: hands wrapped, left palm split and rebound, right dead, staff in the crook of the dead arm, reads by staff only. Sylvanas carries the sacking square, has Tam's teeth marks in two bare fingers, and her left glove is still grey with flour. The Ch4 win is behind them; the network that wastes its watchers is ahead.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: First time inside Sylvanas since Ch3. She saw Jaina's dusk report, the shell, the wards that held, Tam die. She does not know Jaina's private guilt over Tam, that Jaina now thinks 'Sylvanas', or that Jaina doubts the stencil more than she said. Jaina still does not know about Sylvanas's palm on the stone or the circle on the map.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough: the folded square in her coat, or the deep ruts of the grain road. Do not re-run the village.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch from Jaina to Sylvanas, with a short time skip inside the same day (village gate to the first depot office).

craftResearch.findings: Trickle information, raise the question before the answer, and let the detective's questions surface facts. Dense, important interrogation or records scenes can be fractured to raise tension and pace. Do not stop for a research lecture.

The reader must be able to see what the detective sees. Hide the real clue among ordinary detail, never flag it, and give the reader something more interesting on the next line. Withholding the clue is cheating.
Compress travel that carries no story; show distance by a few concrete marks (terrain, weather, hardship); avoid camp routine and filler encounters; skip to the arrival when the journey adds nothing.

A useful setback changes the situation, forces a new decision, reveals character and raises pressure; the strongest midpoint failures come from the protagonist's own flaw. Yes-but and no-and outcomes keep the pressure rising.

pacing.notes: Tension: B1 medium, B2 medium (compressed), B3 medium-high (short), B4 high, B5 medium-high (taut quiet, heavy), B6 high, B6a medium (heavy sequel), B7 medium, B8 low-medium (short), B9 medium-high close. One peak across B4-B6 at 45-65%, with B5's quiet between the two highs, then release and a lift at the close. Scene lengths vary: S1 medium with a compressed middle, S2 long, S3 medium with a short B8. The risk is S1 playing the 'ledgers agree' note twice; B1 is the fit, B2 the scale, B3 the live network.
